difficultyReason: Single causal claim with one obvious alternative explanation. The argument attributes a business outcome to one factor (new marketing strategy), and the correct answer supplies a competing cause (change in consumer preferences) that would account for the result without the claimed cause.
stimulus: A marketing director at a retail chain observed that after implementing a new advertising strategy emphasizing customer testimonials, sales increased by 25% over the following quarter. The director concluded that the new advertising strategy directly caused the sales increase.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most weakens the argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The retail chain had used customer testimonials in advertisements five years prior.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A major competitor closed its store in the area during the same quarter that the new advertising strategy was implemented.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Several employees of the retail chain reported that they appreciated the new advertising strategy.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The advertising budget was increased by 15% at the same time the new strategy was introduced.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Customer testimonials are generally considered an effective form of advertising by marketing professionals.

explanations.correct: This answer provides an alternative explanation for the 25% sales increase that does not depend on the new advertising strategy. If a major competitor closed, the sales increase could result from customers switching to this chain, not from the testimonial-based ads.
explanations.A: Irrelevant historical fact. That the strategy was used before doesn't address whether it caused the recent increase.
explanations.C: Employee appreciation is irrelevant to whether the strategy caused the sales increase.
explanations.D: Actually strengthens rather than weakens. An increased budget might support the argument that the strategy (with more resources) drove sales up.
explanations.E: Supports the plausibility of the strategy working; does not undermine the causal claim.

difficultyReason: Straightforward causal overreach. A physician attributes a patient's improvement to a new medication, and the correct weakener shows the improvement may have a different cause (natural recovery from a viral infection).
stimulus: A physician prescribed an antiviral medication to a patient who had contracted a viral infection. After one week of taking the medication, the patient's symptoms subsided significantly. The physician concluded that the antiviral medication was responsible for the patient's recovery.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most weakens the argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The antiviral medication has been shown in clinical trials to reduce the duration of viral infections by an average of three days.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Most patients infected with this particular viral infection experience a significant subsidence of symptoms within one to two weeks even without treatment.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The patient reported that the medication was easy to take and had tolerable side effects.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Other patients who have taken the same antiviral medication reported improved symptoms within the same time frame.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The patient also received nutritional counseling during the same week she took the medication.

explanations.correct: This answer undermines the causal claim by showing that the observed symptom subsidence is consistent with the natural course of the infection, regardless of medication. If most patients recover on this timeline without treatment, the physician cannot confidently attribute this particular patient's recovery to the drug.
explanations.A: Strengthens by showing the drug does reduce infection duration in clinical settings.
explanations.C: Irrelevant to causation; the patient's experience of side effects doesn't address whether the drug caused recovery.
explanations.D: Strengthens by corroborating the drug's effect in other cases.
explanations.E: Introduces a potential alternative cause, but nutritional counseling is a weaker competitor than natural recovery; (B) is a clearer weakener.

difficultyReason: Simple causal claim about environmental policy with one clear competing explanation. The stimulus attributes increased bird populations to a conservation program; the correct answer shows a confounding factor (mild winters) that could account for the increase independently.
stimulus: An environmental organization implemented a habitat restoration program in a wetland area. Over the next two years, ornithologists observed a 40% increase in the number of migratory birds visiting the wetland. The organization concluded that the habitat restoration program caused the increase in bird populations.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most weakens the argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Migratory birds are sensitive to changes in weather patterns and food availability.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The habitat restoration program involved planting native vegetation and removing invasive species.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The two winters preceding the bird count were significantly milder than the historical average for the region.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Habitat restoration programs in other wetlands have also resulted in increases in migratory bird populations.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The organization's budget for the restoration program was significantly larger than originally planned.

explanations.correct: Milder winters would naturally reduce bird mortality and could easily account for increased populations without any contribution from the habitat restoration. This provides a competing causal explanation that undermines the organization's conclusion.
explanations.A: General background fact about bird behavior; doesn't provide an alternative cause for this specific increase.
explanations.B: Describes what the program did; supports rather than weakens the idea that it could have caused the increase.
explanations.D: Strengthens by showing the program's effectiveness in other locations.
explanations.E: Budget information is irrelevant to whether the program actually caused the bird increase.

difficultyReason: Direct single-cause causal claim in economics. A company attributes profit growth to cost-cutting, and the correct answer shows another factor (increased market demand) explains the profit without relying on the stated cause.
stimulus: A manufacturing company reduced its production costs by 20% through automation and workforce restructuring. The company's profit margin increased by 18% in the following fiscal year. The chief financial officer attributed this profit increase entirely to the cost-cutting measures.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most seriously undermines the argument's conclusion?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The average profit margin in the manufacturing industry remained stable during the same fiscal year.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Industry-wide demand for the company's product increased substantially during the fiscal year.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The automation process required significant capital investment in new machinery and training.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Several of the company's competitors also implemented cost-cutting measures during the same period.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The company's revenues had been declining for three years before the cost-cutting measures were implemented.

explanations.correct: If demand increased substantially, the company would have earned higher profits regardless of cost cuts. This provides an alternative explanation for the profit increase that does not depend on the restructuring, thereby weakening the CFO's attribution.
explanations.A: Irrelevant; other companies' margins don't address what caused this company's increase.
explanations.C: Acknowledges a cost of the program but doesn't undermine the claim that it still increased net profit margins.
explanations.D: Irrelevant; competitors' actions don't explain this company's profit increase.
explanations.E: Provides context but doesn't identify an alternative cause for the profit increase.

difficultyReason: Causal claim in linguistics about language learning. Stimulus attributes improved language proficiency to immersion methodology; correct answer shows the improvement could result from increased study time rather than the methodology itself.
stimulus: A language school introduced a full immersion methodology in which students spoke only the target language during classroom hours. Within three months, the school's students showed a measurable improvement in oral proficiency compared to the previous year's cohort. The school's director concluded that the immersion methodology was responsible for the improvement.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most weakens the argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Students in the immersion program spent significantly more hours per week in structured study than students in the previous cohort.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Some students found the immersion methodology challenging and reported high levels of classroom anxiety.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Immersion methodology has been recognized as an effective approach to language learning in peer-reviewed studies.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The students' native languages are similar in grammatical structure to the target language.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The director had previously taught at another school where immersion was also used.

explanations.correct: If the immersion cohort spent significantly more study hours than the previous cohort, their improvement could result from increased practice time rather than the immersion method itself. This confounding variable undermines the causal claim.
explanations.B: Irrelevant; student anxiety doesn't explain whether the methodology caused the improvement.
explanations.C: Strengthens by providing external evidence for the methodology's effectiveness.
explanations.D: Background information about native-language similarity; doesn't address the causal claim.
explanations.E: Biographical detail irrelevant to the causal conclusion about the current program.

difficultyReason: Straightforward causal claim in technology. A software company attributes user engagement increase to a UI redesign; the correct weakener shows the increase coincided with a marketing campaign that could account for the outcome.
stimulus: A software company redesigned the user interface of its flagship application to be more intuitive. In the month following the redesign, the company recorded a 35% increase in daily active users. The company's product manager concluded that the interface redesign drove the user engagement increase.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most weakens the argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Users generally prefer intuitive interfaces over complex ones.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The company launched a major advertising campaign promoting the application the same week the redesign was released.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Several months before the redesign, the company's daily active user count had been declining steadily.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The company did not change its pricing structure at the time of the redesign.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Some users reported that they found the new interface confusing at first.

explanations.correct: The advertising campaign launched simultaneously with the redesign could fully account for the 35% user increase. This provides an alternative explanation that undermines the product manager's attribution to the UI redesign alone.
explanations.A: General statement about user preferences; doesn't identify an alternative cause for this specific increase.
explanations.C: Provides context about prior decline but doesn't identify an alternative cause for the recent increase.
explanations.D: Absence of a price change doesn't support the UI redesign as the causal factor.
explanations.E: Some initial confusion is irrelevant to whether the overall redesign drove engagement up.

difficultyReason: Simple causal claim in ethics/policy. A hospital administrator attributes a reduction in readmission rates to a new patient-education program; the correct answer shows a competing cause (improved medications) explains the outcome.
stimulus: A hospital implemented a new patient-education program designed to improve patient adherence to treatment plans. Six months later, the hospital's 30-day readmission rate had decreased by 12% compared to the previous year. The hospital administrator concluded that the patient-education program was responsible for reducing readmissions.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most weakens the argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The hospital also increased the frequency of follow-up appointments during the same period.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Patient-education programs have been shown to improve health outcomes in other hospitals as well.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The pharmacy adopted new medications with fewer side effects and better patient tolerance during the same six-month period.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The hospital's staff members received training on the patient-education program prior to its implementation.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Some patients reported that they found the education materials difficult to understand.

explanations.correct: If the pharmacy introduced medications with better tolerance and fewer side effects, this could explain the decreased readmission rate independently of the education program. This competing cause weakens the administrator's causal attribution.
explanations.A: More frequent follow-ups is itself an intervention that could strengthen the education program's effect; however, (C) is a clearer independent explanation.
explanations.B: Strengthens by showing the program's track record elsewhere.
explanations.D: Staff training is part of implementing the program; doesn't undermine the causal claim.
explanations.E: Some patient difficulty doesn't address whether the program caused the readmission reduction overall.

difficultyReason: Single causal claim in history/education. A school principal attributes improved test scores to a new curriculum; the correct answer shows a confounding factor (composition change in the student body) explains the improvement.
stimulus: A high school adopted a new mathematics curriculum emphasizing conceptual understanding over rote memorization. The following year, students' average scores on the state mathematics standardized test increased by 8 percentage points. The principal concluded that the new curriculum was responsible for the improvement in test performance.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most seriously undermines the argument's conclusion?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The state mathematics standardized test is widely recognized as a valid measure of student mathematical proficiency.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A significant number of low-performing students transferred to a vocational school during the same school year.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Mathematics teachers at the school received professional development training on the new curriculum.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Other schools in the district did not adopt the new curriculum and did not experience significant test score increases.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The principal had been an advocate for curriculum reform prior to becoming a school administrator.

explanations.correct: If low-performing students left the school, the remaining cohort would naturally score higher on average, regardless of curriculum changes. This compositional change provides an alternative explanation that undermines the principal's causal claim.
explanations.A: Confirms test validity; supports rather than weakens the argument.
explanations.C: Supports the implementation of the new curriculum and its potential effectiveness.
explanations.D: Strengthens by suggesting the curriculum, not some regional factor, drove the improvement.
explanations.E: Biographical information irrelevant to whether the curriculum caused the improvement.

difficultyReason: Direct causal attribution in arts/cultural policy. A museum director attributes increased visitor attendance to a new exhibition; the correct answer shows a competing cause (holiday season timing) explains the attendance spike.
stimulus: A museum opened a special exhibition of impressionist paintings. In the month following the exhibition's opening, museum attendance increased by 45% compared to the same month in the previous year. The museum director concluded that the impressionist exhibition was the cause of the attendance increase.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most weakens the argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Impressionist paintings are among the most popular art styles with museum visitors.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The museum reduced its general admission fee by 25% during the month of the special exhibition.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The museum's special exhibitions have historically had a modest effect on monthly attendance.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The exhibition opened during the major holiday shopping season, when retail activity and public entertainment visits typically increase.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The museum had hosted impressionist exhibitions twice before, and both had attracted significant attendance.

explanations.correct: If the exhibition opened during the holiday season, when people naturally visit museums and entertainment venues more frequently, the 45% increase could result from seasonal patterns rather than the exhibition's appeal. This provides an alternative explanation.
explanations.A: Strengthens by showing impressionist works would draw interest.
explanations.B: Provides an alternative cause (lower price) for the increase, but holiday timing is a stronger competing explanation.
explanations.C: Weakens the causal claim, but (D) is more directly explanatory.
explanations.E: Strengthens by showing the exhibition type has worked before.

difficultyReason: Simple causal claim in law/criminal justice. A district attorney attributes a crime-rate decline to a new enforcement policy; the correct answer shows a competing factor (demographic shift in the community) explains the reduction.
stimulus: A district attorney's office implemented a policy of aggressive prosecution for minor drug offenses. Within one year, the recorded crime rate in the jurisdiction decreased by 20%. The district attorney concluded that the aggressive prosecution policy was responsible for the crime reduction.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most weakens the argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Aggressive prosecution policies have been criticized by civil rights advocates as unfairly targeting certain populations.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The jurisdiction experienced substantial demographic changes during the same year, with young adults moving out of the area in large numbers.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Other jurisdictions that did not adopt aggressive prosecution policies also experienced crime-rate increases.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The aggressive prosecution policy did not apply to serious felonies, only to minor drug offenses.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Police departments in the jurisdiction also increased patrols during the same period the new prosecution policy was implemented.

explanations.correct: A substantial outmigration of young adults would naturally reduce crime rates regardless of enforcement policies, since younger populations typically have higher crime involvement. This demographic shift provides a competing explanation for the decline.
explanations.A: Ethical criticism doesn't address whether the policy actually caused the crime reduction.
explanations.C: Irrelevant; what other jurisdictions did doesn't explain this jurisdiction's crime decline.
explanations.D: Establishes the policy's scope but doesn't identify an alternative cause for the decline.
explanations.E: Increased patrols might reinforce the prosecution policy's effect; doesn't weaken the causal claim.
